issues.t: High-voltage battery can fail and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a problem. A warning may appear on the dash if the battery overheats while driving, but a fire while parked can happen with no warning at all. Owners under the recall are told to charge only to 80%, so usable range is lower until the fix.
issues.why: Some early battery cells from the supplier can develop an internal short circuit, most likely when the battery is highly charged. Mercedes first tried battery software fixes, then moved to replacing the battery pack on 2022–2024 models; cars built after July 2024 use revised cells.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recalls 25V-050, 25V-894 and 26V-073. Until the repair is done, limit charging to 80% and park outside, away from buildings. The dealer will update the software or replace the battery free.

issues.t: Battery bus bar screws can cause sudden loss of drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The car can suddenly lose drive power while you're driving, with no warning beforehand.
issues.why: A bus bar (a thick metal connector) inside the high-voltage battery may have been fitted with the wrong screws, which can break the electrical connection.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for recall 25V-487. Until it's repaired, park outside. The dealer will inspect the battery and replace it free if needed.

issues.t: Won't start with a high-voltage system warning
issues.sym: The car won't go into drive or 'start', and the dash shows a high-voltage system warning, sometimes along with a red 12-volt battery warning. It can happen right after charging, and some owners see high-voltage warnings while plugged in.
issues.why: Mercedes bulletins point to several causes: a charging error that leaves the high-voltage contactors (heavy-duty relays) stuck closed, or a break in the safety 'interlock' wiring loop from corroded pins, chafed wiring or a loose connector. Warnings about the 12-volt battery are covered by another bulletin.
issues.next: Don't keep trying to start it. Call Mercedes roadside assistance and have it taken to a dealer, and mention the high-voltage no-start bulletins. High-voltage parts are covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile battery warranty.

issues.t: Drive unit and DC fast-charging faults fixed by software update
issues.sym: Drive system warnings, charging interruptions or slower-than-expected fast charging.
issues.why: Mercedes released a software update for 2022–2024 EQBs to make the electric drive unit, the battery management system and DC fast charging more robust. Some owners also report reduced range and slower fast-charging after the battery recall software.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether the drive unit and battery software campaign has been done on your car, and report any range or charging change after recall work.

issues.t: Fault messages when preconditioning or plugged in
issues.sym: Several fault messages show up on the dash when climate preconditioning starts or when you switch the car on with the charging cable connected.
issues.why: The power electronics detect a low-voltage condition while the car is unlocked and store a fault. Mercedes released a software update for the power electronics.
issues.next: Have the dealer install the power electronics software update from the bulletin.

issues.t: Low coolant warning from electric drive cooling
issues.sym: A 'Coolant level too low' warning or coolant indicator light on the dash.
issues.why: Mercedes bulletins link this to the electric drive's cooling circuit, including air getting into the system after certain front drive module replacements, and a stored fault related to the electric motor.
issues.next: Check the coolant reservoir level only when the car is off and cool, and have the dealer look at it under the coolant bulletins rather than just topping it up.

issues.sym: A squeak from the drivetrain when backing up at very low speed, such as under 4 mph.
issues.why: A seal in the electric drive gets damp with coolant while driving forward, and changing direction when reversing makes it squeak.
issues.next: It isn't a safety issue. Ask the dealer about the drivetrain squeak bulletin.

issues.t: Front drive unit gear can fail, risking rollaway (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the gear fails, the car may roll even when in Park.
issues.why: A welded gear in the front electric drive unit may not have been welded properly, so the park lock may not hold the car.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for recall 24V-331; the dealer will replace the front electric drive unit free.

issues.sym: Child seat anchor covers in the second row may not look or fit right.
issues.why: The wrong covers were installed on the second-row child seat anchors, so the car doesn't meet the federal child-seat anchor rule.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-677. The dealer will replace the covers free.
issues.sevReason: Wrong anchor cover parts (labeling); anchors themselves work.

issues.t: Weekly preconditioning schedule missing or grayed out
issues.sym: The weekly climate preconditioning profile is missing from the climate menu or grayed out in the Mercedes me app.
issues.why: Settings in the head unit and powertrain controller software are wrong.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the powertrain control unit software update from the bulletin.

issues.t: Knocking from rear axle on bumpy roads
issues.sym: Cracking, thumping or knocking from the rear of the car over uneven roads.
issues.why: Mercedes found the rear shock absorber mounting may not have been tightened to specification.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the rear shock mounting torque under the bulletin.

issues.t: Brake, parking brake and stability warning lights come on
issues.sym: Warning lights for the brake system, electronic parking brake and stability control light up on the dash.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for these warnings linked to stored fault codes in the brake system.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have a dealer read the codes and check for a bulletin.

issues.t: Steering gets heavier at parking speeds
issues.sym: Steering feels heavier when parking or moving at about 7 mph or less, with no warning message. It can come and go.
issues.why: Power steering assist is partly reduced at low speeds; Mercedes issued a bulletin for it.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the power steering against the bulletin.

issues.t: 'Active Emergency Stop Assist not available' warning
issues.sym: A warning that Active Emergency Stop Assist isn't available, related to the system that senses your hands on the steering wheel.
issues.why: The steering wheel hand-detection system malfunctions and stores a fault.
issues.next: Driver-assist features may be limited until it's fixed. Ask the dealer about the hand-detection bulletin.

issues.sym: Creaking or squeaking from the rear liftgate area while driving.
issues.why: Mercedes traced the noise to the liftgate lock; the root cause was still under analysis in its bulletin.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check the liftgate lock under the bulletin.

issues.sym: Infotainment screen or MBUX functions may not behave as intended; many owners notice nothing.
issues.why: Mercedes launched a service campaign to update the MBUX control unit software on 2024–2025 vehicles including the EQB.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether the MBUX software campaign has been done, or install over-the-air updates when offered.

issues.t: Clunk or noise from drive unit mount on acceleration
issues.sym: A noise when you get on or off the accelerator.
issues.why: Tolerances in the front left mount bearing of the drive unit; Mercedes' fix is to remove the bearing and coat it with anti-seize compound.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the drive unit mount under the bulletin.
